title: Lessons from Manuel Manetta
summary: After first jobs he finds Moneta, a teacher he knew from home, and takes lessons for two or three years; he fetches his book.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Yeah, yeah, yeah. So, so he said, so we wouldn't, we wouldn't take no job. We just rehearsal. So after we, the first job we got, we played for some, oh, Beville Garden, on Beville Street. It rained all day and all night. And then the first job we played for White. That's in, uh, in the Algae area. In the Algae area, right in the Algae, up the Algae, right up the Algae area. Yeah, I know where they are. Yeah. So, all right. And we played, so after that, we, after we, we played there. Well, finally, well, we keep going, so finally, I say, well, I know the man, Moneta, you see? Yeah. From coming out there, my home. See, I never forgot him. And he came in and played in that pavilion, you know? He came in and played in that pavilion one night.

With, uh, some band or nothing. I forgot the name of the band now. But he came there with that band and played. So, and I know him. So, I came down and sort of, I found that he was a teacher. So, well, I got me a book. And I went and took lessons from him. See? So, I took lessons there. I must have took lessons for two, three years, or something like that. And, uh... What kind of books, now?
Book? Wait, I'm going to show you the book.
You still got it? I'll show you the book. See? Charlie, DeGuard told me you studied hard. You should have a little man.
